utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-95-14-R77.4, the Prosecutor versus Marijan Krizic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. May I have the appearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. David Akerson on behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor. I'm here with Rebecca Graham, Salvatore Cannata, and Sebastiaan van Hooydonk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Akerson. For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I am the counsel for Mr. Krizic. My name is Mira Tapuskovic and I am the duty counsel for today. Mr. Krizic has his appointed lawyer, but I'll be acting on his behalf today at his Initial Appearance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tapuskovic. Mr. Krizic -- you must then be Mr. Krizic. I see that you are nodding yes. If you want to say anything, would you please not do it by nodding, because that does not appear on the transcript. So if you push the button of your microphone, you could confirm that you're Mr. Krizic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am Marijan Krizic, and my nodding was just the greeting, since your head was turned towards me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Krizic, if I may introduce myself. My name is Judge Orie. I am a Judge of Trial Chamber I, and your case was assigned to Trial Chamber I by order of the President on the 9th of September of this year. Mr. Krizic, did you receive the indictment that was brought against you in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I received the indictment and I understood it. I did receive it in a language that I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you answered my next question already, that you understood it. Have you had, although perhaps a brief opportunity, to discuss it with your present counsel, Ms. Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have had that opportunity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I would like to invite Mr. Registrar, since it is a relatively short indictment, to have it read in its entirety for you. Mr. Registrar, would you please read the indictment against Mr. Krizic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. The Prosecutor of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, pursuant to authority under Article 18 of the Statute of the Tribunal and Rule 77 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal charges Marijan Krizic with content of the -- [technical difficulty]. --- Break taken at 3.23 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will now resume the Initial Appearance, which was interrupted due to technical problems while the registrar was reading the indictment against Mr. Krizic. Mr. Registrar, could I invite you to restart reading the indictment against Mr. Krizic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The Prosecutor of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, pursuant to her authority under Article 18 of the Statute of the Tribunal and rule 77 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal, charges Marijan Krizic with contempt of the Tribunal, punishable under the Tribunal's inherent power, Rule 77(A), Rule 77(A)(ii), Rule 77(A)(iv) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal. The accused Marijan Krizic. At all times relevant to this indictment, Krizic was editor-in-chief of Hrvatsko Slovo. Charges. Count 1, contempt of the Tribunal. On 16 March 1998, a protected witness testified before the Tribunal in the case IT-95-14-A, the Prosecutor versus Tihomir Blaskic. This testimony was conducted in closed session pursuant to oral orders of the Trial Chamber and a written decision of the Trial Chamber that the witness would testify in closed session and using a pseudonym. On 26 November 2004, the Zagreb-based weekly newspaper Hrvatsko Slovo, published by HKZ-Hrvatsko Slovo d.o.o., printed excerpts of the testimony of the witness and revealed his identity. Hrvatsko Slovo indicated that the issue of 26 November 2004 was the first of ten issues which would feature such excerpts. This publication contravened three existing Court orders: a) The decision of the Trial Chamber I on the requests of the Prosecutor of 12 and 14 May 1997 in respect of the protection of witnesses, dated 6 June 1997; b) The oral order for closed session issued by the Court on the first day of the protected witness's testimony before the ICTY. References to that order are recorded daily on the transcripts of his four-day testimony; And c) The order of the Trial Chamber's Order for the immediate cessation of protective measures for witnesses dated 1 December 2000. From 26 November to 17 December 2004, the publisher of Hrvatsko Slovo was Stjepan Seselj, and the editor-in-chief was Krizic. The 26 November 2004 issue of Hrvatsko Slovo acknowledges that published extracts were taken from transcripts of testimony delivered in non-public proceedings before the Tribunal. The published extracts include an oral order that the testimony be held in closed session. On 1 December 2004, the Prosecutor filed before the Duty Judge an Urgent Motion for an Order for the Immediate Cessation of Violations of Protective Measures. In her Motion, the Prosecutor requested the Duty Judge to issue an Order against HKZ-Hrvatsko Slovo d.o.o., Seselj, and Domagoj Margetic (erroneously believing that he was still the editor-in-chief) to cease publication and to desist from further publication of statements or testimonies of the witness concerned, or of any protected witness. On 2 December 2004, the Duty Judge granted the Prosecutor's motion and ordered HKZ-Hrvatsko Slovo d.o.o. and all its employees, Seselj and Margetic, to cease publication in Hrvatsko Slovo and in any other publications, and to desist from the further publication of statements or testimonies of the witness concerned, or of any protected witnesses. The Republic of Croatia was directed to serve the Cease and Desist Order on HKZ-Hrvatsko Slovo d.o.o., Seselj and Margetic. On 3 December 2004, Hrvatsko Slovo again published excerpts of the closed-session testimony of the protected witness. On 3 December 2004, upon receipt of the Cease and Desist Order, Stjepan Seselj dispatched a letter to the Ministry of Justice, Department of Cooperation with International Criminal Courts, indicating that Hrvatsko Slovo would comply with the Cease and Desist Order. In its 10 December 2004 edition, Hrvatsko Slovo published the Cease and Desist Order, side by side with an article identifying the protected witness again in direct violation of the court order. In its 17 December 2004 edition, Hrvatsko Slovo again published an article identifying the protected witness again in direct violation of the court order. Krizic knowingly and wilfully interfered with the administration of justice by disclosing: a) the identity of a protected witness; b) the extracts of closed-session testimony; and c) the fact that the protected witness had testified in non-public proceedings before the Tribunal. By these acts and omissions, Krizic committed or otherwise aided Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and abetted in the commission of: Count 1: Contempt of the Tribunal, punishable under the Tribunal's inherent power, Rule 77(A), Rule 77(A)(ii), and Rule 77(A)(iv) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Krizic, you'll be called within 30 days to enter a plea on the charges brought against you, but you also may choose to enter a plea today, which might be more practical. I take it that Ms. Tapuskovic has explained this to you. Have you discussed whether or not you want to enter a plea today or to take the period of maximum 30 days with Ms. Tapuskovic? And if so, what did you decide to do?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have discussed the issue with Ms. Tapuskovic and I have decided to enter a plea today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then, Mr. Krizic, I'll read the one and only count in the indictment against you, and I'll invite you to enter a plea on that count. Count 1: Contempt of the Tribunal, punishable under the Tribunal's inherent power, Rule 77(A), Rule 77(A)(ii), and Rule 77(A)(iv) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal. How do you plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Registrar, would you please record the non-guilty plea entered by Mr. Krizic on the one count in the indictment. Mr. Krizic, under normal circumstances, this would be the moment to instruct the registrar to set a date for trial, but there is a motion pending. I do not know whether you're aware of it, but then you're informed hereby that there is a motion pending to join your case with the cases against three other accused, all contempt cases, and a decision has not yet been taken on that motion. The motion has not, at least the OTP has not the intention to bring any change in the charges against Mr. Krizic in this motion, but just seeks the cases to be joined and to have them in one indictment. So therefore, the Chamber will first have to decide upon that motion. Were you aware of the existence of that motion?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have been informed informally about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Tapuskovic, perhaps for practical purposes, since Mr. Krizic, as far as I understand, his counsel from Zagreb is not, at least not at this moment, on the Article 45 list.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you. Just before this Initial Appearance of Mr. Krizic, we have received information from our learned friends from the Prosecution that there is a motion for joining these cases, and I have informed Mr. Krizic that there would be such a motion and that this might cause a certain delay in the beginning of trial in his case. And since Mr. Krizic has already announced that he will have his counsel, I recommended that he should inform his own counsel of that so as to enable his counsel to prepare for his Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, the first thing -- the motion has been filed on the 20th of September. The first thing that should be clear to Mr. Krizic is that if he wants to respond to that motion, that of course he has an opportunity to do so. At the same time, it doesn't seem to be a very complex matter, so if he wants to respond, and since we do not want to lose pace in this case or perhaps these cases together, I would invite Mr. Krizic, and perhaps you could assist him as long as no other counsel has been formally admitted in the proceedings before this Tribunal, to at least let the Chamber know, let's say within a couple of days, perhaps this week, whether Mr. Krizic would oppose against joinder or whether he would not oppose.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, Your Honour. Until Mr. Krizic has chosen his own counsel, I will do my best to protect Mr. Krizic's interests.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore, the Chamber then expects to hear anything from Mr. Krizic as far as his position is concerned not later than this week. And only then we'll know when trial will take place. Mr. Akerson, at the same time, looking at this motion of the 20th of September, and keeping in mind that you did not want to change the charges against Mr. Krizic, I look at the consolidated indictment you wanted to file. And starting with Mr. Krizic under count 2, page 4 of the indictment, it says paragraphs 1 to 13 are incorporated herein by reference. Paragraphs 1 to 13 start to deal with witnesses and protective measures, and then they pay a lot of attention to what happened to Slobodna Dalmacija. I do not know whether you wanted that to be included in the charges against Mr. Krizic. Because it does not appear in the indictment as you have filed it against Mr. Krizic.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: We did intend to include that factually, Your Honour, because we think it's important that, for the Court's understanding, because one of the defences that have been asserted is that this matter has been previously published, and therefore it's public record. And so the context of the earlier publication is relevant on that ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But it certainly is new in the indictment against Mr. Krizic, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: New facts. It's not new charges, though. The charges are exactly the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: And the orders that are described in paragraphs 1 to 13 are exactly the same. The only addition is the factual recitation about the publications that Slobodna Dalmacija had done, had published.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Krizic, so therefore you are hereby informed, and you'll certainly have an opportunity to discuss with counsel the motion for joinder, that the charges against you are the same as proposed now in this consolidated indictment, but some of the background of the publications in other newspapers, Slobodna Dalmacija, and the events surrounding that publication, have been added as, if I do not misunderstood you, Mr. Akerson, as background information for the charges brought against Mr. Krizic.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Just for your information. Having dealt with the indictment and the trial still to come, I'd like to ask the parties, but first the Defence, whether there's any other matter to be raised, any specific personal matters. Ms. Tapuskovic, you know that if any personal matter would be of a character which would not be suitable for a public hearing, that you could ask for --

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. No need to go into private session. The accused has not pointed to the need to go into private session for anything that he might have to say when we discussed the matters before this hearing. Since we have started talking about the joinder of the cases with the other persons who are also held responsible for the contempt of this Court, I would like to say that the accused has been informed about that only informally, and that's why I would like the accused to receive a formal information of that joinder. His counsel will be chosen this week, and he has to be in the position to act in keeping with the Rules. I am going to act on Mr. Krizic's behalf until he chooses a counsel, and if he receives a formal information about the joinder, I will be able to help him in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Registrar, may I take it that a copy of the motion for joinder could be issued to Ms. Tapuskovic this afternoon, so that she can immediately assist her client in understanding it. May I ask a very practical question? Does counsel which Mr. Krizic intends to appoint or have assigned - I do not know what the situation will be - does counsel speak English?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My counsel does speak English. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Ms. Tapuskovic has already mentioned some things. Let me just explain. Since I received the indictment only a week ago, the counsel that I have chosen has not had the time to come to this hearing due to his previous obligations, but he will represent me. He speaks English. I received information informally that there would be a joinder, and this was confirmed to me by Ms. Tapuskovic in our discussion before this hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, this Chamber is not in a position to determine whether or not the counsel you have in your mind would be a counsel that could be admitted under the Article 45 list or whether he could be admitted to act before this Tribunal, but on the assumption that he would, I do understand that he is able to read documents in English. Then is there anything, Mr. Krizic, you would like to add in terms of personal matters to what has been said? And perhaps you could also take the opportunity, and if you would prefer to do that in private session, that's fine, to give us exactly your date of birth and the address at which you can be reached in, as far as I understand, Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was born on 21 December 1955. My address is Granica 60, 10000 Zagreb, the Republic of Croatia. And if I may, I would like to add and ask you: The joinder does not change the fact that the other accused will enter a plea within 30 days, if I have understood you correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two of the other accused have already entered a plea, and the last one has not appeared before this Tribunal and has not entered a plea until now. Whether he will or not, we'll wait and see what the future brings us. So three out of the four have entered their plea. Anything else you'd like to raise?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Tapuskovic, anything to be raised?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Akerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: A couple of very brief matters, Your Honour. We are able to provide disclosure of supporting materials today. However, since the accused does not have the counsel that is going to represent him at trial, we would have to either provide it to Ms. Tapuskovic, who could then provide it to the counsel that would succeed her, or we can provide it directly to the accused. However, in the confirmation of the indictment, part of the Court's order is that no part of the supporting material be disclosed to the accused until further order. So we would need an order from Your Honour that we can go ahead and disclose that supporting material. But in order to expedite the pre-trial process, we would like to disclose it at the earliest possible time, including today in open court, if Your Honour would authorise it. That's the first matter. So I don't know if you want me to go through all the matters or if you want to address that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we'll stick with the first one. Ms. Tapuskovic, would you be willing to receive the supporting material and then do as you see fit, and I'll give an order, an oral order, in which the disclosure of supporting material -- at least, the -- that the disclosure of supporting material is barred until further order will be lifted so that you could discuss the matters, and -- with Mr. Krizic, and could pass it perhaps to his new counsel?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would be willing to do that. I have information that Mr. Krizic, immediately after the end of this Initial Appearance, will want to go back to Croatia. I will take this supporting material over. I will explain to him the procedure, I will tell him what needs to be done with the supporting material so as to enable him to undertake steps and to explain to his counsel what to do with the supporting material. The question now is when the time will start for the preliminary motions, because obviously I'm not going to be his counsel. However, for as long as his counsel is not officially appointed by the decision of the Registry of this Court, in keeping with the Rules of Procedure and Evidence and the instruction on the appointment of counsel, he is actually the person that I have to represent in this case. And I will make sure to warn him about his rights and explain his rights to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Tapuskovic, thank you very much for your cooperation. That's to start with. The preliminary motions, under Rule 72, usually there's 30 days for that. This is a contempt case, which is, in terms of preliminary motions, I would say relatively simple. And since the Chamber wishes very much to proceed as quickly as possible and as reasonable - I specifically add that - the Article 127 gives an opportunity to vary time-limits. It seems reasonable that on an ordinary indictment, where there's 30 days, that ten days for preliminary motions would be sufficient, the ten days to start on the very day that new counsel is admitted by the Registry as taking over your temporary responsibilities.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I believe that this decision of yours does protect the interests of the accused and that it gives his future counsel enough time, irrespective of the fact that this is a rather simple case. And if the counsel decides to file a preliminary motion and irrespective of the fact that this is a simple case, it will leave him plenty of time to do that if he so wishes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ten days would be sufficient. And as far as it has not been clear yet, the order for non-disclosure to the accused has been lifted.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: I have to interject one point --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: -- on that, Your Honour, and that is that it is lifted as far as us disclosing it to the accused and his counsel, but it isn't lifted as far as disclosure to the public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's how I understood your request, that at least the accused has now access to the material, but the non-disclosure to the public remains as it was before.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krizic, this is just for your information that the supporting material is now available to you. But you are not allowed to share it with anyone else than with counsel and, in the future, members of your team, and especially since you are from journalistic circles, it should be clear to you that this supporting material could therefore not be published or discussed with friends, with whomever. So to that extent, the order still stands. It's only you who has now access to this material. Mr. Akerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: And one last point, Your Honour, and that is that if the accused would be willing to provide us with the name and the address of the proposed counsel, it would just allow us to maybe try to speed things up in terms of getting materials prepared for disclosure so that we can keep the trial on track.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Krizic, you're invited to disclose to the Office of the Prosecution the name and the address of your counsel of choice which has not been formally admitted before this Tribunal. Would you be willing to do so?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My counsel is Emil Havkic. And as for the rest of his information, a photocopy has been made of his business card, indicating his address and his e-mail. I don't know who has this photocopy, but somebody must have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may explain. Immediately before my first meeting with Mr. Krizic, I was escorted to the room where Mr. Krizic was sitting. I was escorted by the officials from the OLAD and the secretariat. OLAD is the part of the Registry that deals with the counsel. A photocopy has indeed been made of the counsel's business card, and OLAD will inform the Prosecutor's office at the moment when the counsel is appointed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may add something to this. I Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. have also enclosed a power of attorney for my counsel, and this has also been provided to the Registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Tapuskovic, you said that the information would be -- that OLAD would inform the Prosecutor's office at the moment when the counsel is appointed. Does that mean that the Prosecution could not have yet the address - it has already the name - prior to that? I mean, it could be very practical already to start seeing whether, of course on the assumption that finally Mr. Havkic could be-- or Ms. Havkic, I don't know yet -- would be admitted, to start already first conversations.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, immediately after the end of this Initial Appearance, I will get in touch with the person from OLAD, whom I know personally, and who asked me if I would be willing to take this noble duty to be in the courtroom today at Mr. Krizic's Initial Appearance. I'm going to make a photocopy of that business card and I will call my learned friend and give him that photocopy. I have experience from another case where there were terms by the Prosecutor's office to deliver the supporting material before the appointment, and this was banned by the Registry. However, since I have been appointed here as a duty counsel and somebody to act on behalf of the accused until the counsel is appointed, I don't see a problem for the information on the future counsel to be delivered to the Prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may. I have the business card and I can provide you with the full information. I believe that this would be good at this moment. Mr. Emil Havkic will be my counsel. His office is in Zagreb, Ruzmarinka 31. And I can provide you with his telephone numbers, or maybe that is not important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not important at this moment. The Chamber doesn't need at this moment. We'll just wait and see until Mr. Havkic is formally admitted as counsel. In the meantime, the Office of the Prosecution can act as it deems fit in the expectation of a future appointment or assignment, and it's Ms. Tapuskovic who receives the supporting material at this moment, as acting counsel. Anything else, Mr. Akerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Another matter, Your Honour, and there may be nothing that we can do about it today, but with the pending joinder motion, we're prepared to file a pre-trial brief very quickly. However, because the joinder is pending, we prepared a joint pre-trial brief. We've also had them as separate pre-trial briefs. I was hoping that maybe we could get a time frame from the Court as to when that issue may be resolved, because a lot of issues, or a lot of our work result from that issue being resolved. And you may not be able to provide that, but a general time frame would be helpful to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can tell you that I discussed already with legal officers that a time frame should be established. But it's not easy, apart from all kind of time limits we are still facing, there's also -- there are questions of the composition of the Chamber that will hear the case. Time limits for pre-trial briefs, for responses to that. But we are working at this moment on a time limit, and the mere fact that -- time schedule. The mere fact that I brought the 30-days term for preliminary motions back to 10 days may make it clear to you that time scheduling is not in the back of our mind but in the front of our mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: And I know anecdotally it's been discussed that there may be a trial date in this matter in late October. Is that still the thinking of the Court? Informally, I know, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may be allowed to reply. I understand that the Prosecution is in a haste to complete this case. However, it is a bit premature to start talking about motions at the moment. Rule 65 ter tells us very clearly when preliminary briefs may be filed, and it is only when all the briefs are filed according to Rule 72 and when the other 65 ter submissions are filed, the list of witnesses and the list of exhibits, that is. Therefore, I am not in agreement with the discussion on the possibility to file a pre-trial brief at this moment, irrespective of the form of indictment, that is, whether it's going to be an indictment for Mr. Krizic alone or whether there will be a joinder. I believe that it would be premature to discuss any preliminary motions at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I understood Mr. Akerson's submission to be that they are already prepared to file pre-trial briefs, not to interfere with a non-existing time schedule yet, and that he asked our specific attention for such a time schedule. Of course, we are dependent on many matters, certainly some of the time limits should be changed, should be shortened if we would want to have the trial by the end of October. There are, however, other circumstances which are at this moment not entirely within our control that might frustrate any attempt to have the trial start in the second half of October. So therefore, I can't give you an answer. But if it would be possible to start in the second half of October, we'll certainly not do otherwise, if possible. Because contempt cases are cases that should not take more time than necessary. Usually they are part of an ongoing trial, this of course different here, but at the same time, we are trying to proceed as quickly as reasonable, acceptable.

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: I'd just like to clarify that the only reason we're raising it, we think it's in the accused's interest to know as much of this information, because he's got to plan as well and provide that information to his counsel. And we want to get the pre-trial brief and the other supporting -- and the other disclosure to him so he has as much time to prepare his Defence. And that's why we're anxious to have some sort of time frame so we can actually get on with the rest of the disclosure and our obligations for the pre-trial brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As I said before, there are a few circumstances beyond our control which might be decisive for whether we could still start the trial by the end of October, yes or no. Any other issue to be raised?

utterances.speaker: MR. AKERSON
utterances.text: Not from the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] None from me, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we stand adjourned sine die.
